Rock-bottom is documented as rock (stone) + bottom, originally bedrock and then figurative lowest level. The rock- source marks word-initial position; the component is an English noun in compounds, not a claim that rock- is an inseparable prefix.

Rock-ribbed means having or resembling rock ribs, figuratively steadfast; initial rock is stone, not the unrelated sway verb. The rock- source marks word-initial position; the component is an English noun in compounds, not a claim that rock- is an inseparable prefix.

The adjective means as steady as a rock; restrict to that sense. The Jamaican music genre rocksteady has a separate dance-related history and must not be silently folded into this source meaning. The rock- source marks word-initial position; the component is an English noun in compounds, not a claim that rock- is an inseparable prefix.

Rockbound means surrounded or hemmed in by rocks, from rock + bound. The rock- source marks word-initial position; the component is an English noun in compounds, not a claim that rock- is an inseparable prefix.

Rocklike means resembling a rock, a compound of rock and -like. The rock- source marks word-initial position; the component is an English noun in compounds, not a claim that rock- is an inseparable prefix.

Rocky means containing or resembling rocks and extends figuratively to roughness; distinct from the sway verb. The rock- source marks word-initial position; the component is an English noun in compounds, not a claim that rock- is an inseparable prefix.
